title: Door installation: frame, hinge and fire-door boundary
audience: Door installers and locksmith and door installation workers
learningOutcomes: Check a frame and opening for square, plumb and fixing before a door is hung.
Identify the boundary between standard door installation and fire-door work that must be referred.

instruction.heading: Frame and opening before the door
instruction.body:
A door can only work as well as the frame and opening it hangs in. Before the door is offered up, check that the opening is square, plumb and level. Measure the diagonals of the opening, because a difference between them shows that the opening is out of square. Check the head and the sides for plumb, and the sill or floor for level. Check that the clearances around the door will be even at the hinge side, the latch side and the head. A frame that is racked, twisted or loose causes a door to bind, fail to latch, rub at one corner and wear the hinges early.

Fix the frame to solid structure with fixings suited to the wall material. In timber framing, that means fixings into the studs or noggins; in masonry, it means fixings rated for the masonry and the load. Packing shims help set the frame square and plumb, but they do not hold a frame in place on their own. Pack behind each fixing point so the frame is supported where it is fixed, and then secure the fixings. Check the frame again after the fixings are tightened, because a frame can move as the screws are driven.

Before you hang the door, check its size against the opening, the hinge positions against the frame and the handing of the door. A door hung the wrong way round will not latch in the frame, and a door that is cut to fit an out-of-square opening will look wrong and fail early.

instruction.heading: Hanging, checking and handing over
instruction.body: Hang the door, then check its movement through the full range. Look for even gaps at the hinge side, the latch side and the head. Check that the door opens and closes without binding, that the latch engages the strike cleanly and that the door does not drop or rub at the hinges. Where the door has a closer or a self-closing device, check that it closes the door fully, without slamming and without leaving the door open. Check the lock and any hardware fitted at the same time, and confirm that the lock operates from both sides as the lock type allows. Record the door type, the frame material, the fixings used and the checks made. Hand over with the client's sign-off on the completed work, and state the exclusions in writing.

instruction.heading: The fire-door boundary
instruction.body: A fire-rated door, its frame, its seals, its hinges and its hardware form part of a fire-safety system. The rating is built into the whole assembly, so a door that is fitted in a fire-rated opening must carry the rating required for that opening. The Queensland Fire Department information sheet (version 09/2025) states that fire doors must be self-closing and latching, and that hardware such as closers, handles, locks and vision panels is part of the fire-resistance rating and must be tested and approved by a registered testing authority. The sheet also says that licensed carpenters or joiners can install and repair fire doors, but that only a person holding the Queensland passive fire protection licence for fire doors and fire shutters can certify, inspect or test them (Queensland Fire Department, fire doors information sheet; version 09/2025). This course takes a stricter position than the minimum that the Queensland sheet describes. Refer any fire-rated opening where the rating cannot be confirmed, and refer any work that would change a rated component, such as the hinges, seals or closer of an existing fire door, to a competent specialist. Do not hang a door in a fire-rated opening that does not carry the required rating. Record the door's rating marking where it is visible on the door or the frame, and if the rating cannot be confirmed, refer the job and record that it could not be confirmed.

procedure: Check the opening for square, plumb and level, and measure the diagonals.
Check that the frame will be fixed to solid structure with fixings suited to the wall material.
Set the frame with packing, fix it at each fixing point, and recheck it after the fixings are tightened.
Hang the door and check its movement through the full range, including the latch and any closer.
Identify whether the opening is fire-rated, look for the rating marking, and refer the job if the rating cannot be confirmed.
Record the door type, the frame fixings and the checks made, and hand over with the client's sign-off and the exclusions in writing.

workedExamples.situation: A replacement door is to be hung in a fire-rated opening, and the rating marking cannot be found on the door or the frame.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the door be hung as an ordinary door?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The rating of the opening cannot be confirmed, and a door in a fire-rated opening must carry the required rating. Refer the job to a competent person, record that the rating could not be confirmed, and do not hang the door as an ordinary door. Tell the client what has been recorded and what the referral covers, and do not state that the opening is compliant.

workedExamples.situation: An ordinary internal opening is out of square by a visible amount at the head, and the new door is to be hung in it.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How do you set the frame before the door is fitted?
workedExamples.reasoning: Measure the diagonals and check the plumb of each side. Reset the frame with packing behind the fixing points so it is square and plumb, and fix it into solid structure. Recheck the diagonals and the clearances after the fixings are tightened. Hang the door only when the clearances are even and the latch engages cleanly. Record the measurements and the packing used.

equipmentAndPpe: Spirit level, straight edge and tape measure for checking the opening.
Packing shims and fixings suited to the wall material, including timber and masonry options.
Drill and bits, and eye protection.
Dust mask for cutting timber or masonry, and hearing protection where the task risk assessment calls for it.
Record sheet for the opening, the frame fixings and the checks made.

commonErrors.error: Using packing alone to hold a frame in place.
commonErrors.prevention: Fix the frame to solid structure with suitable fixings, and recheck it after the fixings are tightened.

commonErrors.error: Replacing a fire-rated door's hinges, seals or closer as ordinary work.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer any change to a rated component to a competent specialist, and record the referral.

commonErrors.error: Hanging a door in an opening whose rating is unknown.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the rating from the marking or refer the job, and record the outcome.

commonErrors.error: Checking only the door and not the frame.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the opening, the frame and the fixings before the door is hung, and check the door in its frame after hanging.

commonErrors.error: Assuming the licence position for door installation without checking it.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the state or territory licence position before accepting the job, and record what was checked.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Queensland: the QBCC page states that a licence is needed for building work valued over $3,300, and that some categories of work need a licence of any value (QBCC, who must hold a licence; last reviewed and published 16 April 2026). Lock work is governed by the Queensland security equipment installer position in “Lock types, mechanisms and security-grade selection”.

Victoria: Consumer Affairs Victoria states that domestic building work with a contract value of more than $10,000 requires a registered building practitioner, and that the requirement applies to domestic building work in Victoria (last updated 9 July 2025). Confirm before accepting door installation work in Victoria.

Fire doors: the Queensland Fire Department states that the occupier must maintain fire doors and that certification, inspection and testing needs the passive fire protection licence for fire doors and fire shutters (version 09/2025).
Completing this lesson does not give a carpentry, building, door installation or locksmith licence, and does not authorise alteration, certification or testing of fire-rated doors.

qualityStandard: The opening is checked for square, plumb and level, with the diagonals measured, before the door is hung.
The frame is fixed to solid structure with suitable fixings, and the fixings are recorded.
The door moves freely through its full range, the latch engages cleanly, and the clearances are even.
Fire-rated openings are confirmed or referred, and are not hung as ordinary doors.
documentationEvidence: Opening and frame check record, with the diagonal measurements and the packing used.
Door installation record with the door type, the frame fixings and the checks made.
Referral note for any fire-rated opening, with the rating marking as found or the statement that it could not be confirmed.
Client sign-off on the completed work and the written exclusions.
summary: Check the opening and the frame before the door is hung, and fix the frame to solid structure.
Fire-rated doors and their hardware are referred to a competent specialist where the rating cannot be confirmed or a rated component would change.
Confirm the licence position for door installation before accepting the job.

knowledgeChecks.question: A door must be hung in a fire-rated opening, but the rating cannot be confirmed. What is correct?
options: Hang it as an ordinary door, since the door looks solid enough for the opening
Remove the rating marking so it does not confuse the owner about the door type
Refer the job to a competent person and record that the rating could not be confirmed
Hang it and leave the rating for the owner to check later, once the door is in

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the best way to hold a frame in place?
options: Packing alone, with no fixings, since the packing is firm enough to hold
Fixings into solid structure, after the frame is checked for square and plumb
Adhesive only, with no mechanical fixing at all on the job today
Any screw that happens to fit the hole, since it will hold the frame in place

knowledgeChecks.question: Which check should be done after the door is hung?
options: Confirm the paint colour matches the wall, since the colour is the main concern for the owner
Check that the door moves freely through its range, the latch engages, and the clearances are even
Remove the closer, because it is not needed once the door is hung and the frame is set
Check only the handle finish, since the handle is the part the owner will see most
